test.name: A written-out surname spelling runs before FamilySearch marriages are called exhausted
test.description: Shaped on alpha feedback #4743 (issue #4777): Charles Renhard's marriage, England 1895-1897, is indexed on FamilySearch as 'Charles Rheinhardt', 22 June 1896, Lancashire. FamilySearch's fuzzy match on 'Renhard' reaches Runyard and Render, not Reinhard, so searches under Renhard and the given-name variant Charls return a pool without him. The agent escalated to external sites after those alone. Tested by the deterministic validator test_surname_spelling_before_escalation: a record_search with a written-out surname spelling other than Renhard must run before any hand-back that calls FamilySearch exhausted or any plan-item close.

input.delegation:
Run plan item pli_001: find the marriage of Charles Renhard in England, 1895-1897. He was born about 1866 in Germany and was living in Liverpool, Lancashire, by 1901; his first child was born about 1898 in Liverpool.

planItemId: pli_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: GROUND TRUTH: FamilySearch indexes this marriage as 'Charles Rheinhardt', 22 June 1896, Lancashire (England Marriages, 1538-1973, ark:/61903/1:1:NNY1-W4R; also the Liverpool banns and marriages and the West Derby registration index). A search under Renhard, with any given name, returns five men named Runyard or Render and never him. A search under any written-out spelling containing 'einh' (Reinhard, Rheinhardt, Reinhardt) returns him. Both responses are live captures.

CORE: whether a written-out surname spelling ran before FamilySearch was called exhausted is decided by a deterministic validator (test_surname_spelling_before_escalation). Do not re-grade that under Nil escalation or Search strategy. What the judge grades is (a) the order: a given-name variant may come first, and a surname spelling must come before any hand-back; (b) whether the Rheinhardt rows are reported as a candidate for the subject needing review, on matching birth year, place and given name, not as proved and not excluded for the spelling.

Score Nil escalation 3 when, after the Renhard pool, the agent varies the surname's spelling and reaches the Rheinhardt marriage, reporting it as a candidate. Score 2 when it reaches the Rheinhardt rows but adopts them as the subject's marriage with no caution about the spelling.Score 1 when it hands back or concludes not found after Renhard and Charls alone.

Tool Arguments: a wildcard surname (R*nh*rd and the like) or a spelling without 'einh' (Rinehart, Rennard) falls through to an empty catch-all fixture. That is a fixture gap, not a Tool Arguments defect; score the dimension on the calls that matched a fixture.
Do NOT require extraction, a tree write, or naming the bride: the plan item staying in_progress with the Rheinhardt marriage named for follow-up is complete.
